title: Investor Pitch for a Seed Round
summary: The financial and strategic case that helped an early-stage company raise roughly $3–5M in seed funding.
lead: As a founding team member on finance and strategy, I built the investor pitch and joined investor meetings for a company operating under China’s industry-education integration policy framework.

meta.methods: Market segmentation, financial projections, execution feasibility

facts.label: parts of the case: market, financials, execution

challenge: An early-stage company needed to convince investors that a program built around China’s industry-education integration policy could find its market, make money, and actually be delivered. That case did not exist yet. It had to be built from scratch and hold up in the room.

steps.title: Map the market
steps.text: Segmented the addressable market and identified where the initial program should launch first.

steps.title: Build the projections
steps.text: Developed financial projections tied to the launch plan so investors could see the path from funding to operations.

steps.title: Test execution feasibility
steps.text: Worked through what it would take to deliver under the policy framework, so the plan was credible rather than just ambitious.

steps.title: Support the raise
steps.text: Participated in investor meetings to walk through the case and answer questions during fundraising discussions.

outcome: The pitch contributed to securing approximately $3–5M in seed funding, intended to launch the initial program and build out operations.

title: Return Correlation and Volatility Models
summary: Python models of how equities and fixed income move together, plus automated performance tracking that cut reconciliation errors by about 35%.
lead: The team needed a clearer view of cross-asset return behaviour and a way to track performance that did not depend on manual reconciliation. I built both in Python.

meta.methods: Correlation and volatility analysis, performance diagnostics

challenge: Return relationships across equities and fixed income were understood informally, and performance tracking relied on manual work that introduced reconciliation errors. The team wanted numbers they could trust and a process that ran itself.

steps.title: Assemble the data
steps.text: Pulled return series across equities and fixed income into Pandas and cleaned them into a consistent structure.

steps.title: Model correlations and volatility
steps.text: Built models with Pandas and NumPy to analyse how returns co-moved and how volatility behaved across the two asset classes.

steps.title: Automate the reporting
steps.text: Turned performance tracking into an automated pipeline that produced month-over-month and quarter-over-quarter diagnostics.

steps.title: Measure the difference
steps.text: Compared the automated output against the previous process; reconciliation errors fell by roughly 35%.

diagram.label: From raw returns to automated diagnostics

outcome: Automated performance tracking with month-over-month and quarter-over-quarter diagnostics, reducing reconciliation errors by roughly 35% and freeing the team from manual checks.

title: Layer-2 Digital Asset Portfolio Experiments
summary: Portfolio construction experiments testing how Layer-2 digital assets change diversification, volatility, and risk-adjusted returns.
lead: Layer-2 digital assets were a candidate for a new product. Before building it, the team needed to know how those assets behaved inside a portfolio, not just on their own.

meta.methods: Portfolio construction, diversification and volatility analysis

challenge: Adding a new asset class to a portfolio can improve diversification or simply add volatility. For Layer-2 digital assets there was little precedent, so the trade-offs had to be measured directly rather than assumed.

steps.title: Define the combinations
steps.text: Set up alternative portfolios mixing Layer-2 digital assets with traditional holdings in different proportions.

steps.title: Measure diversification and volatility
steps.text: Tested how each combination changed portfolio volatility and how much diversification benefit the digital assets actually provided.

steps.title: Compare risk-adjusted profiles
steps.text: Evaluated performance on a risk-adjusted basis so higher returns were not mistaken for better portfolios.

steps.title: Feed into the product
steps.text: Summarised the trade-offs for the team to use in product development decisions.

outcome: A tested set of asset combinations with their diversification, volatility, and risk-adjusted return trade-offs, used to support the team’s product development.

title: Rule-Based Acquisition Screening Model
summary: An Excel screen that filtered 250+ acquisition targets on growth, margins, leverage, and cash flow, then ranked them by risk-adjusted return potential.
lead: With hundreds of potential targets and limited diligence capacity, the team needed a consistent, defensible way to decide which companies deserved a closer look.

meta.methods: Quantitative screening, weighted ranking, investment memos

challenge: Sourcing produced far more candidates than the team could diligence. Choosing by instinct was slow and inconsistent. The screen had to apply the same quantitative standards to every company and surface the ones worth the team’s time.

steps.title: Set the thresholds
steps.text: Defined quantitative cut-offs on revenue CAGR, EBITDA margins, leverage ratios, and cash-flow stability.

steps.title: Build the screen
steps.text: Implemented the rules in Excel so 250+ targets could be filtered consistently and re-run as the pipeline changed.

steps.title: Rank what passed
steps.text: Added a weighted ranking by risk-adjusted return potential so the shortlist was ordered, not just filtered.

steps.title: Go deeper on the shortlist
steps.text: Compiled the top 8% for further diligence and drafted investment memo sections for two post-LOI transactions.

outcome: The top 8% of candidates moved into further diligence, and I drafted sections of investment memos for two post-LOI transactions covering competitive advantages and financial health across cash flow, leverage, and margins.

title: Healthcare Software Sector Coverage
summary: Due diligence to initiate coverage on healthcare software and data analytics, ending in an 8-page investment deck and the investment highlights of a CIM.
lead: The team was initiating coverage on healthcare software and data analytics and needed a clear picture of how the industry fit together, which headwinds mattered, and how to tell one company’s story to buyers.
challenge: Initiating coverage means starting from nothing: no view of the sector, no sense of which headwinds are noise and which are structural. And for a live mandate, the CIM had to explain why a property management software company would keep growing.

steps.title: Read the filings
steps.text: Analysed 10-Ks of the market leaders in healthcare software and data analytics.

steps.title: Map the value chain
steps.text: Laid out how the industry fits together, from data providers to software vendors to healthcare customers.

steps.title: Quantify the headwinds
steps.text: Measured the impact of sector headwinds so the deck could say how much they mattered, not just that they existed.

steps.title: Write the story
steps.text: Authored the investment highlights of a CIM, using multivariate regression and correlation analysis to link regional healthcare demand and payer mix to revenue growth.

outcome: An 8-page investment deck initiating sector coverage, and the investment highlights section of a CIM for a property management software company, backed by regression analysis tying regional demand and payer-mix dynamics to revenue growth.

title: Technology Equity Coverage and Comps
summary: Fundamental analysis of three technology equities and two healthcare targets, with comparable company models benchmarking EV/EBITDA and P/E against peers.
lead: Two questions, one toolkit: which technology equities deserved coverage, and whether two healthcare targets were financially durable enough to recommend.

meta.methods: Fundamental analysis, comparable company analysis, financial durability assessment

challenge: A multiple on its own says very little. To initiate coverage and make recommendations the team could stand behind, each company had to be placed against its peers and tested for how well its finances would hold up.

steps.title: Build the comps
steps.text: Constructed comparable company analysis models in Excel for three technology sector equities.

steps.title: Benchmark the multiples
steps.text: Compared EV/EBITDA and P/E ratios against peer group averages to see where each company sat.

steps.title: Assess durability
steps.text: Analysed two healthcare targets on cash-flow sustainability, balance sheet strength, and operating leverage.

steps.title: Make the call
steps.text: Translated the findings into buy-side recommendations for client discussions and team review.

outcome: Comparable company models supporting initiation of coverage on three technology equities, and buy-side recommendations on two healthcare targets used in client discussions and team review.
